results.title: Vision-based autonomous navigation for quadrotor UAVs in unknown and ...
highlights:
Visual Odometry (VO) and Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) are widely studied for UAV positioning and tracking. ORB-SLAM2 (Mur-Artal and Tardós 2017), a well-known lightweight VO algorithm, struggles in low-light conditions, leading to frequent tracking failures. In contrast, VINS-Mono (Qin et al. 2018), the VIO algorithm used in this study, integrates visual and inertial data to provide high-frequency positioning. When visual tracking fails, it compensates using Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data, ensuring higher stability and adaptability. Beyond localization, modern UAV path planning emphasizes trajectory smoothness and adherence to dynamic constraints rather than simple reachability (Zafar and Mohanta 2018). Ego-Planner (Zhou et al. 2020a, b), adopted in this study, optimizes path search efficiency by eliminating Euclidean Signed Distance Field (ESDF) computation, which accounts for 70% of processing time in conventional methods as explained by Usenko et al. (2017). The ESDF-free enables real-time performance in complex environments, making Ego-Planner a state-of-the-art solution. However, its practical adaptability in highly constrained, low-light environments with dense obstacles remains to be further examined.

properties.title: Autonomous Systems: Autonomous Systems: Indoor Drone Navigation
properties.abstract: Drones are a promising technology for autonomous data collection and indoor sensing. In situations when human-controlled UAVs may not be practical or dependable, such as in uncharted or dangerous locations, the usage of autonomous UAVs offers flexibility, cost savings, and reduced risk. The system creates a simulated quadcopter capable of autonomously travelling in an indoor environment using the gazebo simulation tool and the ros navigation system framework known as Navigaation2. While Nav2 has successfully shown the functioning of autonomous navigation in terrestrial robots and vehicles, the same hasn't been accomplished with unmanned aerial vehicles and still has to be done. The goal is to use the slam toolbox for ROS and the Nav2 navigation system framework to construct a simulated drone that can move autonomously in an indoor (gps-less) environment.

results.title: Prisma-Drone-Team/nav2-3D
highlights:
Nav3D is a ROS 2 navigation stack that reformulates the Nav2 architectural model for
three-dimensional UAV navigation. It keeps the parts of Nav2 that are valuable as a
navigation framework, such as action-based task interfaces, lifecycle-managed servers,
plugin-oriented planning and Behavior Tree execution, while replacing the planar costmap
assumption with a 3D collision-aware pipeline based on MoveIt, OctoMap and PX4 offboard
setpoint streaming.
...
The project originates from the master's thesis *Designing a Nav2-Based 3D Navigation
...
Stack for UAVs*. The thesis motivation is practical: ROS 2 has a mature, modular
navigation framework for ground robots, but UAV navigation commonly appears as tightly
coupled planning pipelines or platform-specific systems. Nav3D explores whether a
Nav2-like stack can be preserved at the architectural level while making mapping,
planning, validation and execution consistent with volumetric flight.

Space ROS [10] extends this concept by adding deterministic execution guarantees and radiation robustness specifically for space missions.
